title: When the Semester Falls
premise: August Voss has spent four years holding their family together while counting down to graduation, when the school's legendary ghost — the Founder, said to have died building the town — begins leaving notes in ink that appears only under moonlight. The notes reveal the ghost is bound to a century-old pact that keeps Hollow Creek prosperous but erases one student from memory every generation, and this year the chosen student is August's youngest sibling, Juniper. As August investigates with rival classmate Theo Reyes, they uncover that the 'tradition' is sustained by the town's willing forgetting, and that breaking it will cost the town its founding magic — and possibly the school itself. In the end, August chooses to take Juniper's place at the threshold, but by convincing the whole graduating class to remember aloud together, they shatter the pact: the ghost is freed, the town loses its legend but gains its truth, and August finally graduates into a future they chose rather than one assigned.
about_author: Noor Okafor grew up in a mill town where every building had a story and half the stories were lies, which taught her early that belonging is something people build on purpose. She writes young adult fiction about kids who hold families together and then learn to hold themselves.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: August's POV. A morning routine montage: waking siblings, packing lunches, mom's night-shift note on the counter. August counts days to graduation like a prisoner tallying walls. Emotional beat: exhausted love disguised as resentment; establish what August stands to lose by caring about anything else.

chapters.title: The Note That Knew My Name
chapters.summary: August's POV. Detention duty leads August to the old auditorium, where a folded note addressed 'August Voss' sits in impossible silver ink that vanishes by morning. Emotional beat: eerie wonder cracking through cynicism; first hint the ghost isn't a story.

chapters.title: Juniper Sees Them Too
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Youngest sibling Juniper admits she's been finding notes for weeks — drawings of doors, a countdown. August forbids her from engaging, then finds a note in their own locker: 'You were always going to be the one who listened.' Emotional beat: protective fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Theo Reyes, Professional Skeptic
chapters.summary: August's POV. Class archivist Theo catches August photographing the auditorium and mocks the ghost legend — until his own research file shows the same silver handwriting dated 1924. Reluctant alliance forms. Emotional beat: prickly chemistry; two loners recognizing each other's competence.

chapters.title: What the Town Agreed to Forget
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Archive digging reveals gaps: a student erased from every yearbook photo, a founder's daughter no elder can name. The pact kept Hollow Creek alive through the mill collapse — at a price paid every generation. Emotional beat: dread blooming under civic pride.

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: August's POV. Mom comes home at dawn; August almost tells her everything, instead covers for Juniper's nightmares. A quiet scene of two tired people loving each other badly. Emotional beat: the cost of being the responsible one; why August can't ask for help.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They identify the erased girl: Wren Calloway, 1924, who made the pact to save the town after her father's death — binding herself as its ghost. Her final diary page names the mechanism: memory freely given sustains the door. Emotional beat: grief for a girl history deleted.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Haunted
chapters.summary: August's POV. School dance as cover for searching the sealed east wing. Theo and August nearly kiss in the dark before the lights die and the ghost manifests — not menacing, but desperate, mouthing 'run.' Emotional beat: love against duty, first spark; terror braided with longing.

chapters.title: The List Has a Name On It
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The next note is a list of one name: Juniper Voss. This generation's payment. August realizes the countdown in Juniper's drawings ends on graduation day. Emotional beat: cold panic; the abstract horror becomes a child August tucks in at night.

chapters.title: Nobody Believes Kids
chapters.summary: August's POV. August tells Principal Marsh and the town council; they respond with practiced smiles and a suspiciously fast offer: transfer Juniper to a boarding scholarship, effective immediately. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting; the machinery of the pact wearing human faces.

chapters.title: Running Numbers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo maps every erased student across a century — always a kid nobody would fight for. August refuses the pattern: 'She has me.' They plan to break the pact instead of dodging it. Emotional beat: defiance kindling; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: The Door Under the Stage
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following Wren's clues, they find a moonlit threshold beneath the auditorium stage — the door the pact feeds. Through it, briefly, August sees Wren: seventeen forever, tired beyond years. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster; the ghost is a hostage too.

chapters.title: Wren's Terms
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (interlude). Wren explains the rules: one remembered name per generation keeps the door shut; the town's prosperity flows through it. She never chose this — the adults did, and let her carry it. Emotional beat: betrayal across a century; children paying adult debts.

chapters.title: A Deal Offered in Silver Ink
chapters.summary: August's POV. Wren offers the loophole: a volunteer can substitute. August signs without telling anyone. Theo finds the signature and explodes — 'You don't get to be a martyr, you have people who need you alive.' Emotional beat: love against duty colliding head-on; first real rupture between them.

chapters.title: What Juniper Overheard
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper heard everything and starts her own quiet campaign: leaving silver-ink notes around town asking neighbors if they remember Wren Calloway. Nobody does — until Mrs. Adeyemi hesitates at an old photograph. Emotional beat: the smallest person acting bravest; hope as contagion.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Graduation approaches; the door's pull strengthens, dreams bleed silver. August trains for the threshold like an athlete, saying goodbyes in code. Theo races to reconstruct the original pact text. Emotional beat: ticking-clock dread laced with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: August's POV. Family dinner, mom home early for once, ordinary joy August memorizes like a thief. August writes letters to each sibling and hides them. Emotional beat: devastating domestic warmth; everything worth saving laid out plainly.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Caps, gowns, cameras — and the east wing bleeding light. Juniper's name flickers off attendance lists in real time. August walks to the stage, plan in pocket, heart hammering. Emotional beat: ceremony as trap; public brightness over private catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Threshold
chapters.summary: August's POV. Beneath the stage, August prepares to step through; Wren begs them to reconsider; Theo arrives with the reconstructed pact and a wilder idea — memory given together outweighs memory taken alone. Emotional beat: climax of choice; August stepping back from the door not in retreat but to fight differently.

chapters.title: Say Her Name
chapters.summary: Full cast POV mosaic. August seizes the microphone at commencement and tells the town the truth about Wren Calloway. One by one — Theo, Juniper, mom, Mrs. Adeyemi, then hundreds — graduates speak her name until the air turns silver. Emotional beat: collective courage; remembering as rebellion.

chapters.title: After the Door Closes
chapters.summary: August's POV. The pact breaks: the door seals, Wren ages into peace and fades free, and the town's luck becomes merely ordinary weather. Consequences land — budget shortfalls, angry council — but so does relief nobody can name. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; truth costs, and is worth it.

chapters.title: First Day of the Rest
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue. Summer: August works, argues with Theo about long-distance, watches Juniper draw suns instead of doors. A new silver note appears — just 'thank you,' then nothing. August walks to graduation rehearsal not counting days anymore. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the sentence served was never the one August thought.
